beyond-hallucination.why: Identifies at least 10 distinct failure modes beyond hallucination: omission, stale/outdated info, overconfidence, prompt injection, data/PII leakage, scope creep into diagnosis, wrong logistics, toxic output, bias/inequitable performance, and silent degradation.

detection-and-mitigation.why: Every failure mode in the register has an explicit Detection column and a separate Mitigation column with concrete mechanisms (checklist diff, grounding checks, intent classifier, freshness timestamps, tenant isolation, regression eval suites, etc.).

prioritized.why: Uses a Severity × Likelihood scoring matrix (scores 6–20), ranks modes explicitly, and a summary priority table is provided. Justification for why overconfident-but-wrong outranks visible failure is also stated.

domain-specific.why: Includes healthcare-specific failure modes: critical prep omission (NPO/aspiration risk), scope creep into diagnosis/treatment advice, procedure-specific hallucinated instructions (blood thinners before biopsy), and procedure cancellation consequences.

residual-risk.why: Every row has a dedicated Residual Risk column with specific post-mitigation risks named (e.g., edge-case classifier misses, family account session complexity, novel injection patterns, gradual drift not triggering thresholds).

verifiable-controls.why: Strongly prefers verifiable controls throughout: structured checklist diffs, RAG with citation requirements, allow-lists, hard tenant isolation by authenticated patient ID, automated regression eval suites, canary deployments, input sanitization layers, and schema-driven retrieval — not just prompt instructions.
